name: Appreciation of Women in Media/Literature #5068
description: AWML’s mission is to celebrate, amplify, and explore the voices of women in media and literature while creating an inclusive and supportive community for students to learn, create, and lead. Through discussions, workshops, projects, and events, AWML fosters confidence, collaboration, and self expression, empowering students to tell meaningful stories and contribute thoughtfully

description: We are the Arab Dabke Club and our goal is to build a community of friends that you will have forever and learn the traditional Palestinian Folk Dance, Dabka. name: Arab Pre-Health Association #4715
description: At APHA, we are dedicated to empowering Arab students to thrive academically, professionally, and personally. APHA hopes that in fostering a cross-cultural understanding, we can soon apply that to the variety of health-care professions.

name: Arab Student Association #4350
description: We are the Arab Student Association and our goal is to create and maintain an environment that benefits Arab students and interested members of the community, and to promote an understanding of Arab history, culture, and heritage at the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities. description: The University of Minnesota Archery Program is a student club that is open to participants of all skill levels. Equipment is provided and club officers are NASP certified coaches who are able help anyone from complete beginners to more experienced archers. description: Joining the Art and Drawing Club will allow you to make meaningful connections with other artistic students at UMN while also honing your own artistic skills and learning from others. name: Art Auction @ UMN #5022
description: AAUMN is a student run organization dedicated to fostering a creative and supportive environment for students interested in representing underrepresented Culture and Art including Middle Eastern. name: Art History Club #1674
description: A collective of people who are generally interested in Art History as well as the specifics of local Twin Cities art and art history, in addition to the art of international origins. We also will focus on the interest of learning more about the field through guest lectures and field trips. As well as introducing art history to everyone non-specific to major.

name: Artificial Intelligence Applied #4694
description: In Artificial Intelligence Applied, we are committed to the continual research and general discussion involving the bolstering world of AI. We focus on popular AI models, ethics regarding practices, and implementations across multiple industries. Join us as we delve into the ever expanding industry of AI, and learn about the future of our world while making meaningful connections.

name: Artificial Intelligence Society #4732
description: Our mission is to empower AI enthusiasts with the technical expertise, leadership skills, and business insights to solve real-world problems and drive innovation. name: Artistry of Hmong Dance #4810
description: Our mission is to honor and preserve the rich cultural heritage of the Hmong people through the art of dance. We strive to celebrate the beauty, diversity, and resilience of the Hmong community by showcasing traditional dance forms. Through our performances and cultural exchanges, we aim to foster a deeper understanding and appreciation of Hmong culture while promoting unity, diversity, and inclusivity within our local and global communities. We are dedicated to empowering our members, preserving our heritage, and inspiring future generations to embrace the spirit of Hmong identity through the

description: Artists Collected is a space welcoming fellow artists to collaborate on a project each semester. We welcome all mediums and any expression of art to this club! Check out our Instagram for the semester's project, our first one was creating a Tarot Deck and illustrating the cards!

description: The Arts and Medicine group is a place for medical students and other health professionals to engage with and learn about written, 2D, and performance media from/with their classmates in medicine, and from professionals who have found means of bringing their art into the medical sphere. We aim to celebrate cultural diversity, promote professional development, and build connections through mentorship, networking, and service. While rooted in the experiences of Asian-identifying individuals, we welcome all who share our commitment to cultural awareness, collaboration, and the advancement of oral healthcare.

description: To let Asian students find a place and community where they feel comfortable asking for help from peers and others, and help along their journey through business school! description: Aspiring Educators Twin Cities (University of Minnesota, Twin Cities) shall provide a united voice for all education, leadership in education innovation, dedication to students and families, and an unwavering commitment to the welfare of our members. name: Association of Asian Veterinary Medical Professionals #4581
description: The Association of Asian Veterinary Medical Professionals Student Chapter (AAVMP) aims to inspire, support, and increase the voice and visibility of Asians and Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders (AAPI) in the veterinary profession and advocate for greater general diversity in the veterinary profession.

description: Our mission is to support the academic, social, and career needs of students of African descent in psychology and related disciplines. description: The Association of First-Generation Graduate Students (AFGS) provides a community for individuals who identify as first-generation undergraduate students pursuing a graduate degree. name: Association of Latino Professional For America Twin Cities Student Chapter #4769
description: To empower and cultivate Latinos as leaders of character across every sector of the global economy, our dedicated student organization seamlessly strives to advance Latino leadership by nurturing our members and providing support in their journeys toward excellent opportunities in their chosen industries.

name: Association of Multicultural Scientists #2151
description: Undergrad, grad and professional students are all welcome join the Association of Multicultural Scientists, a space for BIPOC students in STEM! ALP strives to address the substantial need for legal assistance to immigrants, refugees and asylum seekers who seldom have access to legal representation, and increase awareness of these challenges within the University of Minnesota Law School. description: The mission of the Bahá'í Club is to develop our intellectual and spiritual capacities through contributions to positive change in our communities. We do this by engaging in meaningful conversations that introduce us to new ideas and inspire self-reflection, being of service to others and collaborating with individuals and groups that strive to create change on campus, and exploring various religious texts and philosophies to build empathy and respect for others. Bahá'í Faith-inspired materials will guide our efforts to create a culture in which the mode of operation is learning-oriented and p

description: The Energy and Environmental Policy Club (EEPC) will help facilitate discussions, both formally and informally, about current topics in the energy and environmental policy spheres. description: Engineers Without Borders USA builds a better world through engineering projects that empower communities to meet their basic human needs and equip leaders to solve the world’s most pressing challenges. Our main programming usually includes a career panel in the fall, speakers throughout the year, and an Earth Day celebration in the spring, as well as some social events. If someone is interested in joining the group, please email us at eels@umn.edu.

Founded in 2009, UPS is student-governed, and affiliated with the department of Integrative Biology and Physiology, with Dr. Vincent Barnett as our advisor. Although many members are physiology majors, this is not a requirement for membership, and we encourage non-majors to attend our meetings and events. UPS serves to build a community between undergraduate physiology majors, as we

name: Undergraduate Political Science Association #3278
description: UPSA is one of the two student groups under the University of Minnesota's Political Science Department. UPSA serves as the main forum for undergraduate students to voice their opinions and to serve as a resource for helping students to successfully complete their academics. UPSA also serves as the central coordinator of social and community service events for students. UPSA is a non-partisan and non-profit group.

name: Undergraduate Public Health Association #1881
description: The Undergraduate Public Health Association (UPHA) is an organization and resource for students interested in pursuing public health in higher education and as a career! UPHA aims to create awareness of programs and opportunities available within the sector of public health at the University of Minnesota, to provide social/networking events, and to participate in social and academic success on campus. We invite guest speakers, host team building events, and provide volunteer opportunities to connect with like-minded individuals passionate or curious about public health!

name: Undergraduate Statistics Club #3606
description: Stat Club is an undergraduate student-run organization that fosters engagement with statistics beyond the classroom. The club sponsors guest speakers, organizes workshops, and provides networking opportunities with faculty, alumni, and professionals in the Twin Cities. Members have the opportunity to connect with professors and explore the wide range of academic, research, and career paths that statistics can lead to. Founded to support the professional and personal growth of young statisticians, Stat Club strives to build a stronger and more connected statistics community. The board and under

name: Undergraduate Student Government #509
description: We work as the voice of the student body by shaping University policy, working with university administrators and the Board of Regents, and engaging with legislators at every level of government. We believe that all of the students at the UMN deserve to be heard. If you see an issue on campus that needs to be addressed, please let us know here.

name: Undergraduate Surgery Interest Group #3587
description: Our mission is to form a pre-med community by offering unique opportunities for pre-med students such as exposure to the clinical decision making process, hands on surgical experiences, mentorship with medical students, and offering connections with physicians.

name: Undergraduate Women In Business #1444
description: Women in Business is dedicated to bringing together business professionals and students, regardless of major, background, or identities, to network and to learn about a variety of business topics. WIB offers bi-weekly meetings, monthly volunteer events, social events, a mentorship program, and networking opportunities. Women in Business is for the student who wishes to grow personally and professionally while practicing intersectionality connecting and uplifting everyone who identifies as a women. Our members help create a safe, inclusive space for all. WIB also partners itself with businesses

name: Undergraduate Women in Physics and Astronomy #4682
description: We are a group of undergraduate students who are working to provide a safe and fun environment for women and gender minorities interested in physics and astrophysics to connect, talk about physics, and learn more about what the UMN has to offer!

name: Undergraduates Interested In Psychiatry #5049
description: The mission of this club is to help create awareness of mental disorders and to reduce stigmas. This club will expose the members to the study of Psychiatry and its subspecialties (e.g., Forensic, Neuro, Addiction, Child/Adolescent, etc.) Also bringing guest speakers, medical students, and Physicans. With the addition of connecting students with potential shadowing opportunities and more.

name: UNICEF Club at UMN #4608
description: Our organization advocates on behalf of UNICEF: spreading awareness about the challenges children face around the world. From struggling every day to survive, going to school, or escaping conflict and disaster. We also fundraise on behalf of UNICEF Clubs: UNICEF has helped save more children’s lives than any other humanitarian organization. They operate solely on voluntary donations. UNICEF Club at UMN will fundraise in support of children’s survival, access to safe water, nutrition, health care, and protection from violence, exploitation and abuse. On top of that, we volunteer in the communit

name: United Mission for Relief and Development at the University of Minnesota #4239
description: The purpose of this organization is to implement targeted, cost-effective relief and development programs that improve lives. Also, to provide students an outlet for giving, community service, and a global impact on poverty. UMR also wants to raise awareness and support for victims of poverty, catastrophe, and disasters, natural or man-made. We promote, encourage and foster collaboration between similar organizations, student government, and other on-campus and community organizations.

name: United Nations Student Association- Model United Nations (UNSA-MUN) #339
description: This organization is designed to help students understand how the actual United Nations would function and prepare those who are seeking a future career along the UN track while allowing others to understand the chaos of the international world and creativity of simulations. Each year we travel to other collegiate Model United Nations conferences to compete against students from across the nation. At these events, students simulate the United Nations by acting as a nation’s representative to one of the various UN bodies; they debate a variety of issues with other delegates and write resolution

name: UNITY Health #4574
description: Volunteer/Shadow Shadow healthcare professionals who provide primary health care at health clinics across the Twin Cities area that work to eliminate financial barriers. Learn about the communities served and how to improve community health. Take part in community-based medical learning by working with patients in communities that are underserved by the healthcare system in a variety of cultural contexts. Education Provide faculty-led general education workshops about healthcare. Emphasize the importance of practicing equity in medical practice. Promote intercultural competence in pre-health s

name: University Barista and Coffee Club #4707
description: It wouldn't be an overstatement to state that most UMN Gophers run on coffee. Unfortunately, a daily trip to your local coffee shop can do numbers on your bank account. This club will teach students how to create their own caffeinated beverages, while exploring new flavors and introducing a variety of espresso and coffee drinks.

name: University Bible Fellowship #1679
description: Our main focus is to study the Bible, grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and live according to his teachings.

name: University Commercial Real Estate Club #4898
description: Our mission is to provide an educational/networking space for students and professionals interested in commercial/residential real estate.

name: University Cycling Club #454
description: The University Cycling Club is composed of cycling enthusiasts ranging from recreational to competitive racers. All levels are welcome and everyone is encouraged to find a discipline (MTB, Road, Cyclocross, Gravel) and degree of involvement that fits their goals. We strive to include all personnel at the university to engage in the joy of cycling from undergraduate students to university professionals. We also take an active role to promote cycling as a fun, healthy, and environmentally friendly activity within the Minneapolis community and UMN campus

name: University Honors Student Association (UHSA) #2162
description: The University Honors Student Association (UHSA) is a student led group that creates a space for connection and community within the honors programs. Each semester, the UHSA Executive Board plans a variety of events that give honors students the opportunity to relax, have fun, and meet other honors students.

name: University Investment Group #5063
description: Our mission is to educate fellow students on the importance of investing and to help them plan for their future.

name: University League of Legends #2915
description: About In the rapidly-growing field of eSports, League of Legends is the premier title, with over 100 million monthly players! University League of Legends here at the University of Minnesota aims to bring together players who are looking to play the game in a competitive setting, or a casual one. We are looking to build a community through the game with our future events! Some of our activities include giving students the chance to compete in one collegiate competitive teams that play in official leagues against other colleges, holding fun weekly quick in-house games, watching the World Champi

name: University Ninja Club #4107
description: Welcome, prospective ninjas! The University Ninja Club (UNC) is a group for students at the U looking for a fun, physical challenge in a supportive environment. In the UNC you will learn how to beat obstacles featured in the American Ninja Warrior TV series, and in life! All skill levels are welcome, and we encourage everyone to participate in workouts, gym trips, and competitions alike. The UNC has weekly on-campus, ninja-focused workouts, as well as trips to the local ninja gym, Obstacle Academy, at least monthly. Club members can stay updated on UNC events through our GroupMe and Instagram.

name: University of Minnesota ACM Student Chapter #1120
description: We are the Association for Computing Machinery, University of Minnesota, Twin Cities student chapter. We work to promote knowledge and greater interest in the science, design, development, language, management, and applications of modern computing on the Twin Cities campus and around the Twin Cities area. We also host several events throughout the year, including MinneHack (the largest Hackathon in Minnesota), Capture-the-Flag cybersecurity events, and the semesterly UNIX classes! The best way to get involved is to attend events and drop by our room (Keller 2-204) on Tuesdays at 4pm.

name: University of Minnesota Aikido Club #396
description: Aikido is a Japanese martial art with roots in Ju Jitsu. Using body positioning and dynamic motion, an attacker’s energy is redirected into a throw, joint lock, or pin. Emphasis is placed upon the harmonization between attacker and defender to diffuse a conflict peacefully.

name: University of Minnesota American Association of Public Health Dentistry Chapter #5108
description: The University of Minnesota School of Dentistry has a strong mission that aims to guide caring dental professionals. As students at the University of Minnesota School of Dentistry, we have chartered a chapter of the American Association of Public Health Dentistry to help promote the Association’s mission. We have a strong group of students who are passionate about the issues affecting public health dentistry and aim to build a strong chapter in Minnesota, focusing on Policy Literacy, Advocacy Skill Development, Equity, Ethics, and Interprofessional Collaboration

name: University of Minnesota Ballroom Dance Club #391
description: Welcome to the Ballroom Dance Club at the University of Minnesota! For over 30 years, we have sought to spread the love and understanding of ballroom dancing throughout the University community and Twin Cities metro area. Our mission is to create a fun atmosphere for the University and surrounding community. We’re really lucky at BDC to be able to offer professional ballroom lessons! Our club is open to anyone, not just students. We focus on establishing an inclusive environment where dancers return year after year. No special clothing, previous experience, or partner is necessary!

name: University of Minnesota Esports Club #3774
description: Whether you love to play video games casually or competitively, the Esports Club at the University of Minnesota has a place for you! Our club has gaming communities across many different titles including Rocket League, Overwatch, Valorant, and more! Each game supported by the club has competitive teams that play in tournaments against other colleges every semester. They also have casual communities to hang out, chat, and game with fellow fans. The club hosts many casual events every semester, both in-person and online, such as in-house tournaments, watch parties, and more. All are welcome to a

name: University of Minnesota Fencing Club #457
description: Welcome to the page for the University of Minnesota Fencing Club! Whether you've never picked up a fencing blade of you're an experienced veteran, check out the UMN Fencing Club! Join us for weekly practices where we train, skirmish, and compete. Show your gopher pride at various tournaments throughout the semester. Make sure to follow our Instagram to stay up to date! name: University of Minnesota Geological Society (UMGS) #908
description: Hello! We are the University of Minnesota Geological Society-- otherwise known as the "GeoClub". We are a student group that supports and advocates for students in the department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, although anyone with an interest in these subjects is welcome! The GeoClub lounge can be found in the basement atrium of Tate Hall, room B85-- it's a great place to meet ESCI undergrads and other rock nerds. Overall, we host a number of events throughout the school year, ranging from very casual and informal social hours to inviting industry professionals and preparing professional

name: University of Minnesota Handball Club #3641
description: Handball is a sport which promotes the idea of being quick on your feet, reacting to your opponent in a timely manner, and keeping your concentration. These are skills that we are always trying to improve on when we play. Whether it's positioning your feet in just the right place to step into a shot, or coming up with a strategy in the middle of a rally, we try to stay focused on everything going on in the court. Handball also has a very niche, but equally competitive community that strives to improve and hand craft amazing matches.

name: University of Minnesota Men's Club Soccer #62
description: We aim to provide University students with the following: -The ability to participate on a competitive university-based soccer team. -Student leadership development through the club officer positions. -Opportunities to appreciate and apply the values of hard work, dedication, and teamwork. -A positive social environment for students with common interests to meet and learn from one another.

name: University of Minnesota Men's Crew #59
description: Minnesota Men’s Crew is a nationally competitive rowing team open to all students. Most of our team members began with no rowing experience before stepping foot in the boathouse, so we welcome anyone looking to learn something new, work hard in a fun team atmosphere, and reach a level of rowing that challenges even some of the D1 collegiate rowing programs across the country! With a supportive, competitive, and motivating environment, our club strives to help members grow as athletes and individuals. During the school year, our team practices on the Mississippi River in the late afternoon Mond

name: University of Minnesota Men's Gymnastics Club #4442
description: We compete against other teams at both the club and Division I levels, including other Big Ten schools. Our team is a member of GymACT, a national association of competitive club gymnastics teams, which hosts a national championship at the end of the season. We also have daily practices where members can work out together while building a sense of team and community.

name: University of Minnesota Men's Rugby Club #181
description: -We are a competitive sports club which strives to add value in any and every way to each team member’s college experience. -We are a competitive sports club, so we are always training for upcoming competitions against other colleges’ teams. We compete in both 15s and 7s rugby against schools such as Wisconsin, Nebraska, Iowa and Kansas, among others. We also compete in national tournaments in both the fall and spring. -If you are interested in joining the team, we are interested in having you join us. name: University of Minnesota Men's Ultimate Disc Club #467
description: Our mission is to sponsor and organize Ultimate at all levels of competition for all interested members of the University of Minnesota community, and to provide quality fun and competitive opportunities for new and experienced players. This includes a range of activities from non-competitive pickup games to highly competitive intercollegiate and club tournament play. We have three teams as part of our club, with various levels of commitment and competitiveness. Because of this, we cut nobody from our program. name: University of Minnesota Men's Volleyball Club #832
description: To continue a healthy lifestyle by playing competitive volleyball

name: University of Minnesota NeuroNetwork #4665
description: The mission of UMN NeuroNetwork will be to work with students, staff, and faculty within the Neuroscience Department and create an environment that fosters a sense of community and belonging for Neuroscience majors and minors. This will be done by hosting recreational events for students and staff and providing research and volunteer opportunities for students within Neuroscience. Students will be able to interconnect with each other and with the Neuroscience faculty to create a stronger connection and a sense of belonging. We aim to target students from all backgrounds and different interests

name: University of Minnesota Quizbowl Team #2961
description: The team exists to promote trivia-based academic competitions and related pop-culture-based activities among students at the University of Minnesota - Twin Cities. The team does so by organizing and sending teams to a wide range of regional and national intercollegiate tournaments and by hosting intercollegiate, intramural, and high school tournaments in Minneapolis. The team aims to include as many students as possible in its activities while at the same time maintaining its high competitive position on the national academic competition circuit. We will be hosting quizbowl practices in person

name: University of Minnesota Robotics #2467
description: University of Minnesota Robotics is a student organization at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities. We have three major goals: to design and build robots, to support the FIRST Robotics program in the Minneapolis and St. Paul areas, and to host outreach events to raise awareness of robotics and STEM education. Currently, our teams compete Lunabotics, VexU, and Robomaster competitions. Additionally, we participate in non-competitive robot builds, including Robot in 3 Days (RI3D). Outside of competition, we mentor local robotics teams, volunteer at regional events, and facilitate workshops for

name: University of Minnesota Shotokan Karate Club #43
description: About: We teach Traditional Japanese Karate as refined by Sensei Nishiyama, along with Shotoryu Goshinjutsu, the Self Defense system based on the Kata of Shotokan developed by our instructor, David Gimberline. Training in the Shotokan Karate Club allows students to receive the benefits of physical fitness, mental discipline, self-defense, and the challenge of collegiate competition. name: University of Minnesota Sociology Association #626
description: UMSA meets bi-weekly and organizes events that offer useful academic and educational information to sociology undergraduates as well as opportunities for networking with sociology graduate students, staff, and faculty.

name: University of Minnesota Solar Vehicle Project #1465
description: The Solar Vehicle Project is a team of undergrads from many disciplines who accept the challenge to design, build, race, finance and market a solar-powered. The team races in biennial, cross country, intercollegiate competitions, representing the U of M. Since 1991, the UMNSVP has built fifteen vehicles to race cross country events in the USA, along with closed-course events, and international events in Japan, Australia, and Taiwan. name: University of Minnesota Student Chapter of The Society For Theriogenology #5030
description: We strive to provide future veterinarians with experiences to introduce and further their professional careers in the field of theriogenology.

name: University of Minnesota Tae Kwon Do Club #382
description: The Tae Kwon Do Club is a small but dedicated club that provides a space to learn and practice Tae Kwon Do. Additionally, we also teach self-defense, tricking, grappling, and general conditioning. Anyone can join any practice at any date, as long as they show up ready for exercise! Tae Kwon Do is an excellent workout and helps develop both strength and flexibility. We also have an amazing community of members with shared interests, but greatly diverse experiences and backgrounds, inside and outside of Tae Kwon Do. Contact tkd@umn.edu with any questions!

name: University of Minnesota Tennis Club #462
description: Welcome to the official page for the University of Minnesota Club Tennis Team! We are a student-run organization that combines a fun atmosphere with a competitive spin. We encourage all skill and interest levels to come try-out for the 2026-2027 academic year! Please follow our Instagram for the latest pictures and announcements! If you are interested in more information as it becomes available and/or want to try-out, please send us an email at tenniscb@umn.edu and we will put you on our mailing list for updates! Additionally, if your team would like to compete with us, please email us as well

name: University of Minnesota Undergraduate Mock Trial Association #873
description: The University of Minnesota Undergraduate Mock Trial Association is a student organization that competes in intercollegiate mock trial competitions. Each year, students receive a packet of case materials from the American Mock Trial Association (AMTA) and prepare a presentation of both sides of the issue. Students then travel around the state, region, and country competing against other colleges in tournaments. name: University of Minnesota Women's Club Hockey #468
description: About We are the Women's Club Hockey team at the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities. As a team we compete nationally in the American Collegiate Hockey Association (ACHA) Division 2. We emphasize the importance of academics, a balanced college life, and support our players as they prepare for their future endeavors! Visit our website for more information! Meeting Time Tuesday and Thursday nights Meeting Location Ridder Arena

name: University of Minnesota Women's Club Volleyball #1082
description: The goal of this club is to allow students to play competitive volleyball at the collegiate level. We provide the opportunity to continue one's competitive volleyball career without having to commit to a varsity collegiate program. This club is not the same as intramural volleyball as it requires a more experienced level of play. Members of this club can expect to participate in practices twice a week and compete in 3 to 4 tournaments a semester. The teams will travel to the NCVF National Tournament at the conclusion of the spring season. Prospective players are required to tryout for a team.

name: University of Minnesota Women's Rugby Club #1102
description: Our club is a competitive women's rugby team. We welcome everyone, regardless of prior experience or skill level. We strive to provide a holistic, team-oriented experience on and off the field. We work to develop the skills of the individual athlete while also playing with a strong team mindset at a highly competitive level. We create an environment for all our players past, present, and future to grow both as athletes, and as empowered young women. name: University Private Equity Student Group #4851
description: Creating a group where students can learn about private equity and discover more about the industry. Bring in speakers to educate, network, and inform about the industry. Engage in community activities that gives members hands-on experience within the industry and local community.

name: University Women in Film & Television #4774
description: Our group is targeted towards women and gender nonconforming people who are interested in film careers! Our goal is to connect with local film organizations, film festivals, and other organizations who are interested in supporting local film artists. We want to learn how to find networking connections and getting involved in the Minneapolis film industry.

The group provides singers an opportunity to combine their love of singing with meaningful outreach. Urban Sound entertains audiences of both the U of M and Twin Cities area with concerts, events, and benefits. description: The Urological Surgery Interest Group’s mission is to help medical students learn more about urology as a potential career, create connections with urology faculty/residents, and provide opportunities for engagement in research and career advancement. The group hosts a variety of events (e.g. lectures, panel discussions, and skills workshops) throughout the year to achieve these goals.

description: The United States Institute of Theatre Technology (USITT) Chapter here at the University of Minnesota, works closely with the Department of Theatre Arts and Dance. USITT is a student group focusing on theater tech and design, and we seek to supplement skills learned in tech classes and create a supportive network for students. We seek to build our member's professional connections and learning opportunities through sessions with local professionals. If you are interested in receiving updates please email us at usittmn@umn.edu.

name: USlam #4685
description: This student group is open to anyone regardless of major or experience with poetry/public performance. Our goal is to create a community of collaborative writers and a space where members can present their work to a live audience and judges. We provide a Discord server for sharing works, open mic events, a competitive slam once a month, and regular meetings as a space for writing exploration and learning. Our purpose as a club is to be a safe space to engage, learn, and have fun!

description: Engage and mobilize the student body to participate fully in the democratic process through voter registration, education, and advocacy. By providing accessible resources, fostering a culture of civic responsibility, and promoting informed and active citizenship, we aim to amplify the voices of young voters and contribute to a more inclusive and representative democracy. Through collaborative efforts, community partnerships, and grassroots initiatives, we strive to break down barriers to voter participation and inspire meaningful civic engagement among our peers. description: The Veterinary Business Management Association is a national student-driven organization dedicated to advancing the profession through increasing business knowledge, creating networking opportunities, and empowering students to achieve their personal and professional goals. description: To maintain a strong, casual climbing group to help introduce people to the hobby and other climbers along the way, where the key word is casual. We will not be delving into any of the competitive aspects of the sport, and all group funds will be reinvested back into the climbing community.

name: Veterinarians as One Inclusive Community for Empowerment #3615
description: We are the University of Minnesota chapter of VOICE, Veterinarians as One Inclusive Community for Empowerment, an organization that seeks to increase awareness, respect, and sensitivity to differences among all individuals and communities in the field of veterinary medicine. We aim to celebrate diversity within our profession, emphasize the importance of cross-cultural awareness in veterinary medicine, and provide mentorship to youth, particularly those from underrepresented backgrounds, who are interested in careers within veterinary medicine.

name: Veterinary History Club #4677
description: The Veterinary History Club explores and shares the stories of the veterinary profession as well as preserving the history being made today by current students. Our goal is to hold meetings and social events to promote historical topics, as well as establish a student gallery space. We will work alongside the Minnesota Veterinary History Museum in order to engage the College of Veterinary Medicine community and beyond.

name: VeTouch (Veterinary Treatment Outreach for Urban Community Health) #2593
description: VeTouch is a non-profit veterinary student club that provides basic pet care and nutritional support to low or no-income Twin Cities families. The volunteers are veterinary students who also have the opportunity to gain valuable clinical experience while promoting the human-animal bond and establishing a client-veterinary relationship. These students work under the guidance of licensed veterinarians and certified veterinary technicians. We hold clinics on the first Sunday of each month at The Bond Between Food Shelf. description: The Video Game Development Club at the University of Minnesota -- Twin Cities is an academic, fine arts, and hobby club created to fill a demand for video game development on the campus. Our main activity is members forming small groups that work on a project for most of the semester. description: We're Vocal U A Cappella! Vocal U is an a cappella group here at the University of Minnesota that seeks to develop musical talent, to perform throughout the greater Twin Cities area and beyond, and to have fun while doing it. As undergraduate and graduate students from various backgrounds, we connect and bond over our love for music and our passion for spreading harmonies and promoting the arts. At heart, Vocal U is a family-- we motivate each other to be the best performers we can be while supporting each other and having fun together. description: VTrance strives to push beyond the boundaries of what our traditions entail to keep aspects of the Vietnamese culture alive and present for our current generation, as well as those who come after us. We hope to showcase and educate a lesser-known aspect of Vietnamese culture to students and the greater Twin Cities community through a variety of opportunities that will foster memorable experiences.

name: Vyara #5007
description: Vyara is an intercollegiate Indian classical dance competition hosted by the University of Minnesota - Twin Cities (UMN). The name means breath, life force, and flow, reflecting the heart of classical dancers. Through styles like Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathak, and Odissi, dancers share stories of devotion, emotion, and heritage, turning the stage into a living expression of art. Vyara brings together teams from across the country, not just to compete, but to create a space where dancers treat their classical forms as a living language. name: Wallin Scholars at UMN #5095
description: The Wallin Scholars of UMN exists to create a lasting sense of belonging and community for Wallin Scholars. We empower our members by providing peer-led academic collaboration, professional networking, financial literacy resources, and wellness-focused social events. Guided by the Wallin Foundation, we also serve as ambassadors to the wider campus and community through volunteerism and fundraising initiatives.

WAM Collective shall act as a bridge between the widely diverse student body of the University and WAM. The Collective shall foster student ownership of the museum, advise staff on effective ways to engage the student body, and be proactive in promoting WAM throughout the University community and beyond.

name: Well-Being Initiative #4495
description: WBI is a student organization working to improve the well-being of students in Mondale Hall. Our goal is to enact meaningful changes within the law school on both a systemic and individual level by collaborating with faculty and administration to promote institutional and classroom practices that bolster well-being, and by empowering students through well-being focused programming.

name: West African Student Association #5029
description: To create an inclusive and safe space for students to share their culture and traditions and celebrate the culture and traditions of others. In addition to creating a community where people know they are always welcome.

name: White Coats for Black Lives University of Minnesota Medical School Chapter #3776
description: Our mission is to dismantle racism and accompanying systems of oppression in health, while simultaneously cultivating means for collective liberation that center the needs, priorities, and self-determination of Black people and other people of color, particularly those most marginalized in our communities.

name: Widening Access and Valuing Equity in Surgery / Association of Women Surgeons UMN Chapter #4176
description: The Widening Access and Valuing Equity (WAVES) / Association of Women Surgeons UMN Chapter supports medical students traditionally underrepresented in surgical fields who are interested in pursuing careers in surgery by providing exceptional mentorship opportunities with diverse surgeons and allied resident and attending physicians at University of Minnesota. Through lectures, workshops, and mentorship events, we aim to provide an avenue for diverse students and allies interested in surgery to hear from experts and make connections in the field of surgery. WAVES, formerly known as Women in Sur

name: Wilderness Medicine Interest Group #4444
description: This group's purpose is to provide students with the opportunity to learn about wilderness medicine through a variety of workshops, seminars, and hands-on learning opportunities. Additionally, we will use our group to advocate for policies and social causes that make park access, locally to nationally, more equitable, conserve wildlife, and protect the climate. Some of the main activities include workshops on various survival and medical tactics in various climates, split workshops, dangerous and/or venomous plant/animal seminars, advocacy drives, community nights, and other seminars on career

name: Women and Gender Minorities in Mathematics #4671
description: Welcome to Undergraduate Women and Gender Minorities in Math Club! Our purpose is to provide a supportive environment for gender minorities to explore their love of math. Through a variety of events and activities, we aim to expand our members' knowledge and understanding of math.

name: Women in APEC #4908
description: Empowering Women in Applied Economics: Fostering a community of support, advocacy, and professional growth within our department. We are dedicated to promoting diversity, inclusivity, and gender equality, addressing challenges women face in the department. Our mission is to provide resources, mentorship, and opportunities for skill development, creating an environment where all women can thrive academically and professionally. We value collaboration, education, and sustainability, working towards a future where women's contributions to economics are equitably recognized, respected, and celebra

name: Women In Architecture #4945
description: Women In Architecture is a club made to serve the undergraduate women in the architecture program. By building a strong community and fostering collaboration, this club will be a place for friendships to form and professional relationships to begin. A variety of activities including design software tutorials, networking events, firm tours, and study nights will be planned to ensure this mission is followed through.

name: Women In Biological Sciences at UMN #4745
description: Women in Biological Sciences is a welcoming club dedicated to fostering a supportive community for women pursuing studies and careers in biology. Our goal is to provide a platform for networking, mentorship, and personal development. Through workshops, guest speakers, and social events, we aim to empower women in the field, celebrate their achievements, and advocate for gender equality in science. Join us as we strive to inspire and uplift women in biological sciences.

name: Women in Cybersecurity at The University of Minnesota #5109
description: Women in Cybersecurity at the University of Minnesota aims to build a welcoming and supportive community for students interested in cybersecurity while helping women develop the skills, connections, and confidence needed to pursue and advance in the field. We seek to connect students with peers, mentors, academic resources, and industry professionals through networking, education, professional development, and community-building opportunities.

name: Women in Finance #4347
description: Women in Finance is a student organization that is set out to change the stigma and break down barriers impacting women in a historically male dominated field, and to create a sense of community to support women pursuing a career in finance.

name: Women in Healthcare at UMN #4726
description: Our hopes for this student group are that it inspires undergraduate women to pursue a career in healthcare, and connects people who have similar career aspirations and interests! There are so many different types of career options in healthcare and we will be hosting a variety of women who work in healthcare to share their experience, and will also be hosting fundraisers and bonding events!

name: Women in Medicinal Chemistry #4165
description: This student group will operate for the following purposes: 1. To represent the women graduate students in the Department of Medicinal Chemistry in the College of Pharmacy at the University of Minnesota, who wish to participate. 2. To provide support, tutoring, mentoring, career development, and opportunities to create a positive environment within the population of the department 3. To provide social activities and events for members

name: Women Of Color Association #4679
description: The Women of Color Association is a women of color led group focused on creating a reliable and safe space for growing and developing ones personal strengths. We want to inspire, celebrate, and give a safe haven to each and every member. We hold meetings focused on sharing experiences, discussing future goals, and how to reach our goals as women of color. We also invite career professionals to come speak about their experiences, as well hold volunteer opportunities with the Alexandra House and other various non-profit organizations.

name: Women of Color Business Association #4795
description: Our organization strives to create a supporting community for women of color pursuing a career within business. We aim to help our members navigate both academic and professional landscapes by sharing resources, insights, and opportunities, while also providing valuable networking opportunities.

name: Women of Color Collective #4612
description: We aim to create a safe, inclusive, and supportive community-building space for women of color at the University of Minnesota Law School.

name: Women of Color in Stem #4508
description: To provide a support group and safe space for students in STEM majors, not limited to, but specifically for students who identify as women of color. To provide social activities and events for the members and create opportunities for members to express and explore different cultures. To provide K-12 outreach opportunities and create relationships with the local communities.

name: Women's Club Lacrosse #793
description: The Gopher Women's Lacrosse team is a competitive team participating at the D1 WCLO level. We travel throughout the metro, state, and country to play against teams, develop our lacrosse skills, and build team chemistry. We value hard work, competitiveness, and creating a positive team environment. We welcome players of all ages and are excited to continue our success in the 2026-2027 season!

name: Women's Dental Association #2686
description: The University of Minnesota Women's Dental Association (WDA) is here to serve and empower women in our community; educate ourselves on topics including salary and contract negotiation, identify strengths and promote yourself through resumes, work life balance and family planning, workplace harassment, and financial education. We plan to host lunch and learns as well as possible evening events, fundraisers, and weekend outreach events. name: Women's Law Student Association #42
description: WLSA is an organization of law students dedicated to addressing the role of gender and the law, particularly the effects of legal doctrines and practice on issues related to gender. All are welcome!

name: Women* In Medicine #2164
description: WIM* Mission statement: University of Minnesota Women* in Medicine is a community of UMN medical students and professionals united in the advancement of anyone who experiences disadvantages due to their gender, including individuals who are cisgender, transgender, gender-non conforming, or identify within a gender minority. WIM* strives to empower medical students in their professional pursuits, advocate for gender equity, and share in education. WIM* welcomes all students passionate about our mission of promoting gender equity in medicine, irrespective of sex and gender identity.

name: Womens Volleyball League #4916
description: At Women's Volleyball League, we are a volleyball community at the University of Minnesota dedicated to creating a fun, low-pressure environment for students who love the game but aren’t looking for high-commitment athletics. Whether you played competitively before college or just love the sport, our league offers a space to stay active, build friendships, and connect through volleyball. We play 1–2 times a week, cheer on Gopher volleyball together, organize team bonding events, and share our passion for the sport—on and off the court.

name: World Cafe #4573
description: The World Cafe Student group works to create world cafe style events in which students may join to have conversations on topics that may be uncomfortable in order to spread awareness. It will be a guided conversation in about certain topics/issues that concern our campus, state, and country. This group is here to make uncomfortable conversations comfortable as speaking about an issue is the first step in making a difference.

name: Xi Chapter of Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc. #3901
description: The Brothers of Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc. hold friendship as our core value. This can be seen in the motto of our fraternity which is “Friendship is Essential to the Soul”. The four cardinal principles of our fraternity are Manhood, Scholarship, Perseverance, and Uplift. We are also involved in community service opportunities as well.

name: Yelling for History Club #4090
description: The Yelling for History Club is a student group at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities which hosts fun historical roleplaying megagames where players immerse themselves in the personalities of key characters during pivotal events of world history, for the purposes of entertainment and education. It’s like DND with less dice, but more roleplaying! We believe that immersion in these historical scenarios provides context and an enhanced understanding of the time period, as well as allowing students to view the relevant issues from the perspective of those who were involved in the controversie

name: YOUmatter at UMN #3975
description: My group is called YOUmatter, a mental health awareness club on campus. It works to give students a safe space to connect with other students on the basis of discussing mental health and acts as an outlet to distress with different events and meetings. Some of our meetings are more educational regarding topics around mental health awareness (therapist coming to speak at a meeting, different mental health related services on campus coming to share their information, etc.), while others like our off campus "outings" serve to provide wholesome bonding activities for students (a trip to the farmer

name: Young Adult Optimist Club #5160
description: By providing hope and positive vision, Optimists bring out the best in youth, our communities, and ourselves. To develop optimism as a philosophy of life utilizing the tenets of the Optimist Creed; to promote an active interest in good government and civic affairs; to inspire respect for the law; to promote patriotism and work for international accord and friendship among all people; to aid and encourage the development of youth, in the belief that the giving of one’s self in service to others will advance the well-being of humankind, community life and the world.

name: Young Democratic Socialists of America at the University of Minnesota - Twin Cities #4413
description: Our mission is to educate and organize students on the UMNTC campus to play a helpful and principled role in the movement for social justice. We seek a socialist future that extends democracy into all aspects of life -- social, political, and economic. We are involved in various student and labor efforts on campus that are aligned with this future, such as political education events, collaborative events, community outreach, protests, and more.

name: Young Life College - Twin Cities #2185
description: Younglife’s mission is to introduce adolescents to Jesus Christ and help them grow in their faith.​

name: Youth Movement Against Alzheimer's Disease of the Twin Cities, Minnesota #4979
description: Our aim is to reduce the stigma associated with Alzheimer’s disease and dementia by promoting disease education, providing opportunities to connect and support those affected by the disease, and inspire a generation of youth to take action to protect their own brain health by learning about and practicing brain healthy habits. We also recognize the growing community of students who are providing or helping to provide care to someone living with Alzheimer’s and aim to support caregiving youth with a range of resources and programs.

name: Yu-Gi-Oh! Club #2547
description: The Yu-Gi-Oh! Club is a club that provides a place where players of the Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game (TCG) can meet and hang out. Our mission is to provide a safe, secure, and fun place for University of Minnesota students to play the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG. We also occasionally host casual club tournaments. The Yu-Gi-Oh! Club meets every Friday in Coffman Memorial Union Room 326 from 3:00-8:00pm, with tournaments typically starting no later than 5:00pm if they occur. You can stop by at any time to get involved with the club, as we always have open dueling available. We hope to see you there! Most annou

name: Zamorano Alumni Association at the University of Minnesota #5082
Zentopia: Find Your Balance #4867
description: Zentopia is dedicated to fostering mental health awareness, promoting mindfulness practices, and enhancing the well-being of students at the University of Minnesota - Twin Cities. Our mission is to create an inclusive, supportive, and safe space where students can connect, share their experiences, and learn about mental health resources. Through education, community-building, and advocacy, we aim to promote a culture of empathy, understanding, and self-care on campus.

name: Zero Burn at the UMN #5061
description: Making UMN students aware of where their waste goes and what they can do about it.

name: Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Incorporated #2756
description: The mission of Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Inc. is to promote the ideals of service, scholarship, charity, sisterhood, civil and cultural endeavors, and finer womanhood

name: Zoo, Exotic, Aquatic, and Wildlife Medicine Club (ZEAW) #1008
description: Our mission as the Zoo, Exotic, Aquatic, and Wildlife Medicine Club is to promote education in all aspects of non-traditional species. Our club is designed to give veterinary students who are interested in pursuing exotic medicine access to lectures from current clinicians, wet labs to get hands-on experience, and field trips to exotic programs around the Twin Cities. We strive to have at least 1 lecture and 1 wet-lab/field trip every month provided for students. Since UMN CVM does not have a full exotic program, our club gives students the chance to apply what they have learned about other sp

name: Zoobiquity #4393
description: Zoobiquity works to foster interprofessional communication, collaboration, and learning among students in different health professions about what is shared between human and animal medicine. Zoobiquity stimulates future health professionals to ask, “do animals get ___? Do people get ___?” and generates unique perspectives for any career in the healthcare community. All health science students are welcome.
